name: Should I choose a tub or a bigger shower?

mainEntity.name: Should I keep a tub or replace it with a bigger shower when changing the bathroom layout?
mainEntity.text: Should I keep a tub or replace it with a bigger shower when changing the bathroom layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: This decision depends on how the bathroom is used and how much space the room can realistically give up. A bigger shower can make a bathroom feel more luxurious and practical, especially in primary suites where daily comfort matters more than having a tub. A tub can still be the better choice in family homes, guest bathrooms, or resale-sensitive projects where buyers may expect at least one bathtub in the home. The layout should not force a tub into a space where it creates awkward circulation or squeezes the vanity too tightly. Homeowners should consider the long-term use of the house, not just the current trend. In many cases, the best solution is the one that improves the room’s function without sacrificing flexibility.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a tub if the home needs family use, resale flexibility, or a second bathing option. Choose a bigger shower if the bathroom is used mainly by adults and the current tub makes the room feel cramped or outdated.
